points.reason: The block stores and changes busy when a DMI operation is accepted or dmi_rsp_i.ack arrives, and a stuck busy value prevents new requests from being accepted.
The block samples the unchecked jtag_tms_i command into the TAP synchronizer, while reset or a stalled clock can clear or prevent the sampled command from reaching the TAP controller.
This block only copies tap_sync.tms_ff to a wire at line 110 and provides no independent observation, modification, or blocking mechanism.
The sampled TMS value selects every TAP state transition, so an altered sequence can select incorrect scan behavior or hold the TAP in reset, pause, or another state that withholds transfers.
The rising-edge pulse gates TAP state transitions, so withholding it can stall processing of the TMS command.
The TMS-derived TAP state selects whether instruction or data registers capture, shift, or drive JTAG output, so a wrong state changes or blocks the intended scan operation.
The TAP state decides whether the update trigger is generated, so an altered state can dispatch an unintended update or prevent a normal DMI update.
